title: FOR THE DIFFICULT | Pearls of Wisdom from Kyriakos Grizzly
summary: The first Pearls of Wisdom episode reads three Kyriakos Grizzly catchphrases as life philosophy. For the difficult means seeking hardship over results, mogging means surpassing yourself rather than others, and you have to live it means making lifting a lifestyle. NH ties all three to rejecting modern comfort and to the spiritual side of lifting.
claims: Memes that last carry a hidden meaning; Kyriakos Grizzly's catchphrases hide real wisdom behind the screaming
Over-focusing on results makes people ignore the journey and never reach the results; the results are the by-product of doing it for the difficulty
The lifters who stick with it and get the best physiques and strength are the ones who stopped caring about results and lifted for the challenge itself
Complaining that life is difficult signals a wrong mentality; a man should first embrace difficulty and then seek it out
Difficulty gatekeeps gains from those who do not deserve them; if building muscle were easy it would lose its value, just as rarity makes gold precious and rocks cheap
Easy pleasures like porn and masturbation are destructive cheap thrills, while gains earned through hard work give far more joy and pride
He believes in lifter supremacy: lifters put the body back at the centre of development, which makes them a rare breed
Mediocrity is found in avoiding difficulty
For the difficult also means rejecting modern comfort and seeking out the tiger, the challenges the modern world has removed and shames men for wanting
Mogging is mostly a pursuit of self-improvement; comparison and competition are healthy sources of motivation, not toxic
Lifters who only aim to beat a specific person stop once they get there; aim to surpass yourself, because your potential is not limited by others (Pierre Bottero quote)
Follow your own vision instead of copying someone exceptional; even a perfect plan was crafted for someone else, not for you
Hobbyists stay mediocre; to get really good at lifting you have to make it a lifestyle
The marketed bodybuilding lifestyle of pre-workouts, clothes, trendy gyms and selfies was designed to sell supplements
Lifting made him better in every aspect of life; before lifting he describes himself as mediocre
Training half-heartedly to avoid getting too bulky gives no results at all, not even toned
Depressed and miserable men are those with no difficulty in their lives; people are restless because their soul is not being tested
